nodes.label: stdio transport
nodes.rationale: The backend is connected before the transport, so a wrong credential or unreachable backend fails at startup with a diagnosis on stderr rather than on the first tool call.

nodes.label: A tool returns its payload; BaseHandler does the rest
nodes.norm_label: a tool returns its payload; basehandler does the rest
nodes.rationale: BaseHandler.handle() owns dispatch, timing, the MCP envelope and error mapping; building the envelope in a handler nests JSON inside JSON because serializeResult passes it through.

nodes.label: Never write to stdout
nodes.rationale: stdout carries MCP protocol frames over stdio; anything else corrupts the stream and breaks every tool at once. dotenv 17 did it, which is why index.ts loads it quiet.

nodes.label: Amethyst Keeps Externally Added modlist Entries
nodes.community_name: Research: Linux, MO2 under Proton, Platform, Local Models
nodes.norm_label: amethyst keeps externally added modlist entries
nodes.rationale: Each GUI save re-reads under a lock and prepends unknown lines, but writes known lines from memory, so an external flip or reorder of a known line is lost.

nodes.label: Safe Amethyst Write (new mod folder + prepend +Name)
nodes.community_name: Research: Linux, MO2 under Proton, Platform, Local Models
nodes.norm_label: safe amethyst write (new mod folder + prepend +name)
nodes.rationale: Amethyst has no refresh IPC or watcher; add a new mod folder, prepend +Name and add *Plugin.esp, then the user presses Refresh and Deploy; never write into Data because restore moves unknown files to overwrite.

nodes.label: Case-Insensitive Lookup, Dedupe by Realpath
nodes.community_name: Research: Linux, MO2 under Proton, Platform, Local Models
nodes.rationale: On a default CachyOS install nothing is case-insensitive; every lookup in Data, mods and overwrite compares lower-cased relative paths and dedupes case-alias symlinks by realpath.

nodes.label: ICU Requirement (.NET globalization)
nodes.community_name: Research: Linux, MO2 under Proton, Platform, Local Models
nodes.rationale: The helper is deliberately not globalization-invariant because Mutagen's YAML writer formats with the en culture; on Linux .NET fails to start without ICU.

nodes.label: Three Bindings, One Shape (Windows MO2, MO2 under Proton, Amethyst)
nodes.community_name: Research: Linux, MO2 under Proton, Platform, Local Models
nodes.norm_label: three bindings, one shape (windows mo2, mo2 under proton, amethyst)
nodes.rationale:
All three have mods/, overwrite/ and profiles/

/{modlist,plugins,loadorder}.txt; they differ only in where settings live (ModOrganizer.ini vs paths.json + deploy_state.json) and in * semantics.

nodes.label: One list of handlers (createHandlers)
nodes.rationale: What the server serves, the reference documents and the contract tests check must be one list; never keep a second.

nodes.label: Per-session rate limit (token bucket)
nodes.rationale: One agent in a loop looks exactly like healthy traffic from the front and can take a shared backend down for everyone.

nodes.label: Errors must be McpError and name the next step
nodes.community_name: Errors must be McpError and name the next step
nodes.norm_label: errors must be mcperror and name the next step
nodes.rationale: A raw Error reaching the client becomes an opaque Internal error; a model reads the message and acts on it.

nodes.label: References written as FormIDs only
nodes.rationale: Spriggit never writes the editor ID beside a reference, so reading and writing a project needs an editor-ID/FormID lookup.

nodes.label: CI helper build and check
nodes.rationale: Builds the plugin helper for each system and starts it once: checks its protocol and a version read from a version resource, which on Linux is the helper's own parser.

nodes.label: CI smoke test step
nodes.rationale: Drives the built server over real stdio and fails on anything but JSON-RPC frames on stdout, which no unit test can see; given a nonexistent SKYRIM_MO2_INSTANCE because a runner has no game, so it starts and healthcheck reports the instance unreadable.

nodes.label: Plugin helper (C# .NET process on Mutagen)
nodes.rationale: Every plugin read and write goes through one .NET process built on Mutagen (ADR-0003); the server talks to it in JSON lines over stdio; building it needs the .NET 10 SDK.

nodes.label: Test instance (portable MO2 on a clean game, or throwaway Amethyst profile)
nodes.norm_label: test instance (portable mo2 on a clean game, or throwaway amethyst profile)
nodes.rationale: The server writes mod folders, mod order and load order; a Wabbajack-installed instance deletes every mod it did not install on its next update.

nodes.label: GPL-3.0 license
nodes.rationale: The plugin engine Mutagen is GPL-3.0, so the whole project follows it (ADR-0006).

nodes.label: Write paths run against a real backend once
nodes.norm_label: write paths run against a real backend once
nodes.rationale: A fake accepts any order of calls so it cannot know the backend's own rules; what is learned is then encoded as an assertion so the fake enforces it.

nodes.label: No container image
nodes.rationale: The server reads the instance, the game's plugins and a Papyrus compiler from disk and runs the .NET helper beside itself; a container reaches none without identical bind mounts and cannot see a running mod manager.

nodes.label: Linux setup with Amethyst
nodes.rationale: With Amethyst open, deploy asks for Refresh then Deploy, because deploying behind its window would race it.

nodes.label: Per-session bearer token (SKYRIM_ACCEPTED_TOKENS)
nodes.rationale: Each caller's token becomes that session's identity and one backend is built per session, so two people never share one credential; with no remote API behind it, the token list is the whole authority.

nodes.label: Mod Organizer under Proton (experimental)
nodes.rationale: Deploy refuses while this instance's Mod Organizer runs, because MO2 holds the profile in memory and writes it back on exit and cannot be told to re-read it under Proton.

nodes.label: OpenClaw registration (skills, agent, workspace)
nodes.rationale: OpenClaw reads no server instructions and hides MCP tools behind Tool Search for a local model, so setup registers skills, an agent with thinking on and a workspace; behind Tool Search the agent took two to three times the turns.

nodes.label: Path settings read as a POSIX shell would
nodes.norm_label: path settings read as a posix shell would
nodes.rationale: Neither .env nor a client's env block passes through a shell, so ~ and variables are expanded by the server itself, relative paths taken from the server's folder; %VAR% and $(...) are refused.

nodes.label: Session bound to its token
nodes.rationale: A session id is a routing key, not a credential; only a digest of the token is kept.

nodes.label: TLS terminated in front of the server
nodes.norm_label: tls terminated in front of the server

nodes.label: Creation Kit
nodes.rationale: Stays for what only it can do (placing objects, navmesh); its work is pulled back into the text.

nodes.label: npm run setup (setup program)
nodes.rationale: Installs the .NET 10 SDK if missing, builds server and helper, finds the mod manager and asks only for what it cannot find, registers with Claude Code, Claude Desktop, VS Code and OpenClaw, ends with a healthcheck; asks before anything it installs, downloads or registers.

nodes.label: Papyrus compiler (Creation Kit's or russo-2025's)
nodes.rationale: The Creation Kit's compiler needs .NET Framework 3.5 on Windows and does not run on Linux, where russo-2025's papyrus-compiler is used.

nodes.label: First-pull normalisation of Bethesda plugins
nodes.rationale: A plugin saved by Bethesda's tools is normalised once on first pull (translation order, negative zeros, NumRecords/NextFormID) and stable after, so pull and deploy can compare text without false alarms.

nodes.label: Spriggit Translation Packages (NuGet)
nodes.rationale: Text output is stamped with package and version so old text deserialises with the old package; first use needs nuget.org and the .NET SDK.

nodes.label: Mutagen Binary Overlay Import Mode
nodes.rationale: Only fields that are accessed get parsed; the mod object returns almost immediately and the GC can free records; trade-off: repeated access re-parses.

nodes.label: GPL Mere Aggregation (separate processes)
nodes.rationale: Pipes, sockets and command-line arguments between separate programs normally keep them separate works, while linking makes a combined work; GPL code (Mutagen, libloot) is best kept in a separate process from the MIT server.

nodes.label: CETCompat false for MO2 Compatibility
nodes.rationale: MO2 does not play well with the .NET 9 CET feature, so the csproj sets CETCompat to false.

nodes.label: Mutagen Passthrough Correctness Tests
nodes.rationale: Import, re-export and byte-compare after normalisation to prove read/write correctness.

nodes.label: xEdit Has No Windowless Mode
nodes.rationale: SSEEdit is a Delphi VCL GUI; script and automation modes still open the main window and exit via -autoexit.

nodes.label: Papyrus Compiler Options on Linux (by fidelity)
nodes.norm_label: papyrus compiler options on linux (by fidelity)
nodes.rationale: No maintained byte-identical Linux compiler release exists today; ordered by fidelity: CK compiler in the prefix with .NET 3.5 or Mono, papyrusc 4.0 once released, russo's compiler now.

nodes.label: Local models through Ollama
nodes.rationale: Ollama defaults to a 4k context below 24 GiB VRAM; the model must make real tool calls (gemma4:26b and e4b do, code-completion models write calls as text).

nodes.label: Claude Code Behind Ollama (tool search off, 4,096-char cut)
nodes.norm_label: claude code behind ollama (tool search off, 4,096-char cut)
nodes.rationale: Tool search is disabled behind a non-first-party ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, so every MCP tool loads upfront; the core profile and the response budget matter most there.

nodes.label: Ollama Default Context by VRAM
nodes.rationale: Default context is 4k below 24 GiB VRAM, so the server's instructions should not assume 64k.

nodes.label: oterm
nodes.rationale: stdio children inherit only six basic env vars, so server configuration must be declarable in env or a config file.

nodes.label: qwen2.5-coder:3b Writes Tool Calls as Text
nodes.norm_label: qwen2.5-coder:3b writes tool calls as text

nodes.label: AGENTS.md (guidance for agents working on the repo)
nodes.norm_label: agents.md (guidance for agents working on the repo)
nodes.rationale: Docs are kept accurate deliberately: a contradiction between doc and code is a bug in one of them, fixed rather than worked around.

nodes.label: Tool reference (generated)
nodes.rationale: Rendered from the tool definitions themselves so it cannot drift from the code.

nodes.label: Record every local-model eval round
nodes.rationale: Transcripts show where a model wastes calls because of the server (a relative path joined to the wrong folder, a misspelled type answered with nothing found); fix those in the server for every client.

nodes.label: Tool reference generated; router hand-written
nodes.rationale: toolDocs.test.ts fails on a stale reference; the router holds intent phrases a generator cannot infer.

nodes.label: Full Paths in addPatch/buildProject Answers
nodes.rationale: gemma4 joined plugin-relative file names to the project folder and failed every patch run; full paths in the answer gave the shortest route findRecords, addPatch, read_file, edit_file.

nodes.label: Flat Argument Schemas, No JSON-Schema Keyword Names
nodes.norm_label: flat argument schemas, no json-schema keyword names
nodes.rationale: gemma4 drops parameters named type/description/properties/required and oneOf arguments need coercion, so schemas stay flat with no root oneOf/anyOf.

nodes.label: No Terse local Tool Profile
nodes.rationale: The measured losses were not about the tool list; fixes that help every client (full paths, arguments sent as text taken as their declared type) went in for all.

nodes.label: addPatch misused to make new records
nodes.norm_label: addpatch misused to make new records
nodes.rationale: Seven of e4b's eight round-21 misses copied a vanilla record with addPatch and renamed it; the warning came after status success and was passed by.

nodes.label: AGENTS.md workspace file carrying server instructions
nodes.norm_label: agents.md workspace file carrying server instructions

nodes.norm_label: backslash at a line end refused as a copied escape

nodes.label: Claude Code as the eval client
nodes.norm_label: claude code as the eval client
nodes.rationale: Built-in tool schemas were 135 KB of the first prompt's 159 KB; denying unused built-ins and side traffic took the first prompt from 41,652 to 7,757 tokens. Replaced by OpenClaw on 2026-10-18.

nodes.label: Local model eval harness (eval-ollama, eval-openclaw)
nodes.rationale: Runs the tasks through the built server against the instance in .env and checks each against the instance itself, never against values written into the script.

nodes.label: Eval tasks: find, read, filter, patch, build, sword, spell, npc, note
nodes.norm_label: eval tasks: find, read, filter, patch, build, sword, spell, npc, note

nodes.label: OpenClaw as the eval client
nodes.rationale: The client the user chats through, run headless on the user's configuration; its model discovery had set num_ctx to 32,768 and thinking is off for local Ollama models unless configured.

nodes.label: Round 20: hints that give the line to write
nodes.norm_label: round 20: hints that give the line to write

nodes.label: skyrim modding agent (OpenClaw tool allow list)
nodes.norm_label: skyrim modding agent (openclaw tool allow list)
nodes.rationale: The allow list takes the first prompt from 26,093 tokens to 7,219; thinking max is sent as think high.

nodes.label: Text refusals say what stays as it is
nodes.norm_label: text refusals say what stays as it is

nodes.label: No-escapes-copied check
nodes.rationale: Copying a JSON string as it reads leaves doubled backslashes or escaped quotes (e4b did so in rounds 12-13); the note task was built to show it.

nodes.label: OpenClaw Tool Search hides MCP tools
nodes.norm_label: openclaw tool search hides mcp tools
nodes.rationale: With Tool Search on, 26b never found the server's tools and each call costs a search, a description and a call; turned off globally.

nodes.label: Thinking-off measurement: leave thinking on
nodes.rationale: Thinking off saved 41% of the time but lost 16 of 42 tasks (e4b 41/42 to 25/42); generated tokens, mostly thinking, are where the time goes.

nodes.rationale: On install or update every file the modlist does not account for is deleted, except downloads, saves and paths with a [NoDelete] component.

nodes.label: MO2 Overwrites External Edits on Exit
nodes.norm_label: mo2 overwrites external edits on exit
nodes.rationale: On exit MO2 writes modlist and plugin files from in-memory state; the safe external edit is to close MO2, edit and restart, or edit with no pending changes and immediately trigger refresh.

nodes.label: Adding a tool is a one-file change
nodes.community_name: Adding a tool is a one-file change
nodes.norm_label: adding a tool is a one-file change
nodes.rationale: getTools(), the router, tools/list and the contract tests all derive from toolSpecs(), so a listed tool is always callable and always tested.

nodes.label: DelayedFileWriter 200 ms pending window
nodes.rationale: Refresh clobbers an external edit only if the user changed the mod list in MO2's UI less than 200 ms earlier; otherwise MO2 re-reads from disk.

nodes.label: MOMultiProcess: one primary MO2, commands forwarded
nodes.norm_label: momultiprocess: one primary mo2, commands forwarded
nodes.rationale: A second ModOrganizer.exe sends its command line to the system-wide primary, fire-and-forget; -p guards the profile but -i cannot tell two portable instances apart.

nodes.label: MO2 does not watch profile files
nodes.norm_label: mo2 does not watch profile files

nodes.label: Detect a running MO2 instance by process image path
nodes.norm_label: detect a running mo2 instance by process image path
nodes.rationale: MO2 creates no run-lock file; compare each ModOrganizer.exe's full image path with the instance directory; selected_profile in ModOrganizer.ini is only a hint.

nodes.label: Mod file version metadata (name, version, file_category)
nodes.norm_label: mod file version metadata (name, version, file_category)

nodes.label: Mod pages cannot be created through the API
nodes.norm_label: mod pages cannot be created through the api

nodes.label: MO2 overwrites external edits on launch and exit
nodes.norm_label: mo2 overwrites external edits on launch and exit
nodes.rationale: OrganizerCore::beforeRun and the destructor call saveCurrentProfile, so an external edit not followed by a refresh is lost when the user launches anything or closes MO2.

nodes.label: update_mod_version flag
nodes.rationale: Without it the mod page's headline version does not change (DaymareOn/hdtSMP64#374).

nodes.label: v3 upload flow: session, PUT, finalise, poll, add version
nodes.norm_label: v3 upload flow: session, put, finalise, poll, add version

nodes.label: Research: Nexus publishing API and MO2 refresh semantics
nodes.norm_label: research: nexus publishing api and mo2 refresh semantics

nodes.label: Nexus API Acceptable Use Policy
nodes.rationale: Personal keys are tolerated for personal use; keys must not be used without a user-initiated action; so MCP uploads must be user-initiated, and a distributed tool should register with Nexus.

nodes.label: Nexus Terms of Service (sections 10-11)
nodes.rationale: Bans bots, scrapers and automated devices on the site, so uploads must go through the API rather than by driving the website.

nodes.label: Plugin order chosen by mtime (loadorder.txt vs plugins.txt)
nodes.norm_label: plugin order chosen by mtime (loadorder.txt vs plugins.txt)
nodes.rationale: GamebryoGamePlugins::readPluginLists picks the order by mtime, so an external tool should write both files consistently, or write only plugins.txt and leave loadorder.txt older.

nodes.label: refresh launches the GUI when MO2 is not running
nodes.norm_label: refresh launches the gui when mo2 is not running
nodes.rationale: RefreshCommand::runPostOrganizer returns and main goes on to app.run(), so a tool must check MO2 is running before calling refresh.

nodes.label: Docs and skills served to clients at runtime

nodes.rationale: The docs are part of the product, served as MCP resources and through readServerGuide/readSkill; guides.test.ts reads the real files so moving a doc without updating GUIDES fails the tests.

nodes.label: Operating-system and mod-manager seams (ADR-0007)
nodes.community_name: Docs and skills served to clients at runtime
nodes.rationale: What differs by operating system and by mod manager sits behind two separate seams; code that differs by system belongs only in platform.ts, and its Linux side is tested on Windows too.
